scholarships.title: NSF Graduate Research Fellowship Program (NSF GRFP)
scholarships.official_source: U.S. National Science Foundation (NSF), Division of Graduate Education

existing.description: The NSF GRFP funds full-time graduate students pursuing research-based master's or doctoral degrees in NSF-supported STEM fields at accredited, nonprofit U.S. institutions. Each fellowship provides three years of financial support over a five-year fellowship period: a $37,000 annual stipend paid to the fellow and a $16,000 annual cost-of-education allowance paid to the institution in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees, so there is no tuition or mandatory-fee cost to the student. There is no post-graduate study service requirement, and fellows may transfer to a different institution after completion of the first fellowship year. Estimated 1,500 awards for the 2027 solicitation (NSF 26-526), pending availability of funds.
eligibility: At the time of submission, must be a U.S. citizen, national, or a permanent resident ("green-card" holder).
Must intend to enroll or be enrolled full-time in an eligible research-based master's or doctoral degree program in an eligible field of study in STEM.
Must never have previously accepted an NSF Graduate Research Fellowship.
Must have declined any previously offered NSF Graduate Research Fellowship by the deadline (if applicable).

Must have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program according to the institution's academic calendar; non-degree coursework must be clearly identified in the transcript and does not count toward this limit.
Must not be a current NSF employee.

Degree programs must be at a nonprofit institution of higher education accredited in, and having a campus located in, the United States, its territories, or possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
An eligible applicant can submit only one application per annual competition.

Fellowships may only be used for an eligible graduate degree program at a nonprofit academic institution accredited in, and having a campus located in, the U.S., its territories, possessions, or the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico.
existing.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be U.S. citizens, nationals or permanent residents who will enroll full-time in an eligible research-based master's or doctoral STEM program and have completed less than one academic year in a graduate degree program.
benefits: Five-year award with three years of financial support.
Access to supplemental funding to sustain research while on medical leave.
Access to professional development opportunities and the NSF GRFP community.
The fellowship is portable and can be transferred to a different institution of higher education; fellows can transfer after completion of the first fellowship year.
coverage: $37,000 stipend paid to the fellow for each of the three years of financial support.
$16,000 cost-of-education allowance provided to the institution of higher education in lieu of all tuition and mandatory fees for each fellow using the support in a fellowship year.
Access to professional development opportunities and the NSF GRFP community.
Access to supplemental funding to sustain research while on medical leave.
requirements: Prepare and submit the application in the GRFP Application Module on Research.gov.
Create a Research.gov account to access the module.
Provide accurate personal information: full legal name, mailing address, permanent address, date of birth, high school location, and demographic information.
Select a level (Level 1 undergraduate, or Level 2 graduate) in the application.
Provide the list of institutions, enrollment status, enrollment dates and degree conferred (if applicable) for all degree-granting undergraduate and graduate institutions attended.
Provide significant academic honors, fellowships, scholarships, publications and presentations.
Select the Major Field of Study most closely aligned with the proposed graduate program and research plan; the Major Field of Study determines the application deadline and the reviewers.

Request reference letters in the GRFP Application Module and rank them in order of preference; three reference writer names and contact information are required, and two reference letters must be received by NSF.
Provide a Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement of a maximum of three pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
Provide a Graduate Research Plan Statement of a maximum of two pages with headings for Intellectual Merit and Broader Impacts.
Reference letters are due before the NSF GRFP application deadlines, by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on the reference letter date in the Notice of Funding Opportunity.
All materials are submitted through the GRFP Application Module; emailed and/or physically mailed applications will not be accepted.
Applications are automatically checked by the GRFP Application Module for compliance with the format requirements; documents that are not compliant will not be accepted by the module.
documents: Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement (maximum three pages).
Graduate Research Plan Statement (maximum two pages).
Graduate transcripts, if applicable; these may be unofficial if the institution of higher education does not provide official transcripts for first-year, first-academic-term graduate students.
Two reference letters (the module allows a request for up to five reference letters; if more than three are received, the top three are considered).
Three reference writer names and contact information.
Completed application package submitted in the GRFP Application Module.
application_method: Create a Research.gov account if you do not already have one.
Access the GRFP Application Module, which usually opens in July or August.
Select your eligibility level (Level 1 or Level 2).
Enter education, work and other experience, including all degree-granting institutions attended.
Upload official undergraduate transcripts in PDF format, and graduate transcripts where applicable.
Select the Major Field of Study and subfield that is most closely aligned with the proposed graduate program and research plan; this fixes your deadline and reviewer panel.

Enter the names, organizational affiliations and email addresses of three reference writers, ranked in order of preference, and submit the request; reference writers are notified by email with instructions.
Draft and upload the Personal, Relevant Background, and Future Goals Statement (three pages maximum, PDF only).
Draft and upload the Graduate Research Plan Statement (two pages maximum, PDF only).
Receive at least two reference letters by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on October 16, 2026.
Submit the completed application package in the GRFP Application Module by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time on the deadline for your Major Field of Study (October 19, 20, 22 or 23, 2026).
Track your application status in the GRFP Application Module; NSF typically notifies applicants in the spring.
existing.selection_notes: Applications are reviewed by disciplinary and interdisciplinary scientists, engineers and STEM experts selected by NSF Program Officers, with care taken to ensure no conflicts of interest. Applications are reviewed in broad areas of related disciplines based on the Major Field of Study selected by the applicant, using the two NSF Merit Review Criteria: Intellectual Merit (potential to advance knowledge) and Broader Impacts (potential to benefit society and contribute to specific, desired societal outcomes). Intellectual Merit factors include the ability to plan and conduct research, work independently, work as part of a team, interpret and communicate research, take initiative, think creatively, solve problems, persist and overcome challenges, and demonstrated intellectual ability as indicated by grades, coursework and awards. Broader Impacts factors include increasing participation in STEM, improving STEM education through outreach and mentoring, increasing public scientific literacy, increasing collaboration among academia and industry, improving educator development, improving societal well-being, developing a globally competitive STEM workforce, improving national security, increasing U.S. economic competitiveness, and enhancing research and education infrastructure. GRFP was established to recruit and support individuals who demonstrate the potential to make significant contributions in STEM.
existing.best_fit: Final-year undergraduates, bachelor's degree holders with no prior graduate degree enrollment, joint bachelor's-master's students in their final undergraduate or first graduate year, and first-year graduate students in their first research-based graduate degree program, who are U.S. citizens, U.S. nationals or permanent residents.
existing.notes: No post-graduate study service requirement. Fellowship funds are awarded to the institution of higher education at which the fellow is enrolled, and the institution is responsible for disbursing the stipend to the fellow; the fellowship is therefore only usable at an eligible accredited nonprofit U.S. institution. The fellowship period is five years with three years of financial support, so fellows must plan for two unfunded years. Fellows may transfer to another institution after completing the first fellowship year. Practice-oriented professional degree programs (medical, dental, law, public health, MBA, MPH, MSW, JD, MD, DVM, DDS) are excluded at any time during the fellowship, as are joint science-professional degree programs. Applicants may submit only one application per annual competition, and only in the first year of their first graduate degree program (joint bachelor's-master's students are limited to one application). No clinical or medical-school pathway is eligible.
existing.duration: Five-year fellowship period with three years of financial support
existing.application_period: The GRFP Application Module usually opens in July or August; applications for the 2027 competition close between October 19 and October 23, 2026 depending on Major Field of Study, with reference letters due October 16, 2026. The module opened in time for the 2026 application cycle; the 2027 application deadlines were published August 25, 2026.
existing.deadline_display: Reference letters due October 16, 2026 by 8:00 p.m. Eastern time. Application deadlines: October 19, 2026 (Life Sciences); October 20, 2026 (Computer and Information Science and Engineering; Materials Research; Psychology; Social Sciences); October 22, 2026 (Engineering); October 23, 2026 (Chemistry; Geosciences; Mathematical Sciences; Physics and Astronomy). All applications must be received by 8:00 p.m. Eastern Time on the deadline date for the Major Field of Study selected. November 15, 2026 is the last day to withdraw an application without it counting towards the number of times an individual may apply.

existing.description: Google PhD Fellowships directly support graduate students as they pursue their PhD.
eligibility: Enrolled full-time in a PhD programme in computer science or an adjacent field at an accredited research institution that awards research degrees to PhD students
Nominated by the student's university during the application window; direct applications are not accepted
Must remain enrolled full-time in the PhD programme for the duration of the Fellowship or forfeit the award
Google employees, and their spouses, children and members of their household, are not eligible
Students already supported by a comparable industry award are not eligible; government or non-profit organisation funding is exempt
Past awardees from the PhD Fellowship programme are not eligible to apply again

Region-specific stage requirements, for example Canada and the United States require completed graduate coursework by the academic award year, and East Asia requires most graduate coursework completed
existing.eligibility_summary: PhD students in computer science or an adjacent field at an accredited research institution that awards research degrees, nominated by their university during the application window. Direct applications from students are not accepted.
benefits: Africa: up to 3-year Fellowship of US $15K to cover stipend and other research related activities and travel expenses including overseas travel
Australia and New Zealand: 1-year Fellowship of AUD $20K to cover stipend and other research related activities and travel expenses including overseas travel
Canada and the United States: up to 2-year Fellowship of US $85K per year towards education costs (tuition and fees), living expenses, travel and personal equipment
East Asia: 1-year Fellowship of US $10K to cover stipend and other research related activities and travel expenses including overseas travel

Europe and the Middle East: up to 2-year Fellowship with a yearly bursary towards stipend or salary, health care, social benefits, tuition and fees, conference travel and personal computing equipment, varying by country
India, early-stage PhD students: up to 4-year Fellowship of US $50K; India, late-stage PhD students: 1-year Fellowship of US $10K
Latin America: up to 2-year Fellowship of US $15K per year to cover stipend and other research related activities and travel expenses including overseas travel
Southeast Asia: up to 3 years of US $10K per year, or up to graduation whichever is earlier

requirements: Be nominated by an eligible university; direct applications from students are not accepted
Submit all materials in a single, flat (not portfolio) PDF file
Submit a research proposal of maximum 3 pages excluding references
Meet the region-specific student stage requirement
Submit before the regional application deadline, as late submissions are not reviewed and extensions are not granted
documents: Student CV with links to website and publications, if available
Research or dissertation proposal, maximum 3 pages excluding references
Transcripts of current and previous academic records
Two to three letters of recommendation from those familiar with the nominee's work, at least one from the thesis advisor for current PhD students
Cover sheet signed by the Department Chair confirming the student passes eligibility requirements, for Africa, Europe, the Middle East, Canada, East Asia, the United States and Latin America
One-page CV of the student's primary PhD advisor
Region-specific student essay responses of up to 350 words each for Canada, East Asia, the United States and Latin America
existing.english_requirement: All application materials should be submitted in English.
application_method: Contact your department or graduate school about the university's internal nomination process
Be nominated by an eligible university during the application period
The university submits the application on the student's behalf through the portal, which becomes available on the programme page when the application period begins
Upload a single flat PDF containing all required materials
existing.selection_notes: Applications are evaluated on the strength of the research proposal, research impact, student academic achievements and leadership potential. Proposals should align with Google AI Principles. A nominee's status as a member of a historically marginalized group is not considered. Incomplete proposals will not be considered. Universities may nominate up to four students in Canada and the United States, up to three in Africa, Australia, New Zealand, East Asia, Europe, India, Southeast Asia and the Middle East, and any number in Latin America.
existing.best_fit: Promising PhD candidates in computer science or an adjacent field at accredited research institutions worldwide, nominated by their university, with a strong research proposal aligned to Google's research areas.
existing.notes: Monetary awards are paid directly to the Fellow's university for distribution with no overhead assessed. Fellowship recipients do not become Google employees and the award does not increase the chances of a Google internship or job. Fellowship recipients are not subject to intellectual property restrictions unless they complete a Google internship.
existing.duration: One to four years depending on region: Africa up to 3 years, Australia and New Zealand 1 year, Canada and the United States up to 2 years, East Asia 1 year, Europe and the Middle East up to 2 years, India up to 4 years for early-stage and 1 year for late-stage PhD students, Latin America up to 2 years, Southeast Asia up to 3 years.
existing.application_period: Annual cycle. The 2026 cycle ran from March 5, 2026 to April 30, 2026. Google has not published the dates for the next cycle. Google PhD Fellowships begin at the start of the upcoming school year after award notification.
existing.deadline_display: Applications are currently closed for the 2026 cycle. Applications open March 5, 2026; applications close April 30, 2026; notification of proposal decisions by Aug. 31, 2026; public announcement of new fellowship recipients by Oct. 31, 2026.
existing.program_type: Industry-sponsored international doctoral fellowship awarded through university nomination.
